newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian Hansapank boosts Q1 profit.
newsitem.headline: Estonian Hansapank boosts Q1 profit.

text.p: Hansapank, the largest bank in Estonia and the Baltic states, on Monday said its first quarter consolidated group net profit rose to 136.1 million kroons from 52.2 million kroons.

The bank said in a statement that the profit was made up of income at its bank business of 96.4 million kroons, 21 million kroons in leasing, 6.9 million kroons at its Hansabank-Latvija subsidiary, 8.4 million kroons at its asset management company and 300,000 kroons in insurance.
The remainder came from minor affiliated companies.
The bank's group net interest income rose to 180.8 million kroons from 69.3 million and assets climbed to 8.65 billion kroons from 3.84 billion.
The results were well-received by dealers and the bank's shares rose to a high of 288 kroons from Friday's 269.50 close. It later settled at around 280 kroons.
"The group figures are very good," Sander Danil, analyst with Tallinna Pank, said.

"If you take out extraordinary items such as the profit from share trading at the beginning of the year and the sale of the stake in Hoiupank, the subsidiaries' share of the profit is still quite large," he added.
